title: DecoRTL: A Run-Time Decoding Framework for RTL Code Generation with LLMs
problem: LLM-generated RTL code suffers from hallucinations, repetitions, and syntax errors due to low confidence in structurally complex or semantically ambiguous regions.
motivation: Improving RTL generation correctness and diversity enables practical AI-assisted hardware design without manual code review.
method: DecoRTL uses syntax-aware temperature adaptation and self-consistency sampling: generates multiple candidates, re-ranks by token agreement, and adjusts sampling temperature per token role (low for syntax-critical, high for exploratory tokens).
key_novelty: Inference-time decoding strategy differentiating syntax-critical vs. design-critical tokens, using contrastive sampling without model fine-tuning.
contributions: Empirical analysis of token-level entropy during RTL generation identifying confidence issues
Self-consistency sampling for promoting correctness with diversity
Syntax-aware temperature adaptation mechanism per token role
Inference-time solution with no model fine-tuning required

metrics.accuracy: improved syntactic validity and functional correctness
metrics.other: improved output diversity on VerilogEval benchmark

limitations: Evaluation limited to open-source LLMs and VerilogEval benchmark; does not address semantic correctness beyond functional testing.
